## Claims

### C-R7-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, acts-paul-tensions]
- **claim:** Moo rejects Hays’s claim that destination/date is “almost entirely irrelevant for interpreting” Galatians: only the broad thrust is unaffected; specific verses and Paul’s life/theology development are strongly affected.
- **quote:** "The specific sense of many verses is affected by the issue; and it has very important implications for our understanding of the course of Paul’s life and ministry"
- **locus:** L15615
- **passage:** (note on Intro: destination/date)

### C-R7-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]

- **quote:** "Breytenbach (1996: 101–3) notes a tendency for German scholars to favor… the North Galatian view, while British and American scholars are more divided."
- **locus:** L15623
- **passage:** (note on Intro: North/South Galatia)

### C-R7-007
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo’s three-point NPP assessment: (1) Dunn/Wright rightly seek first-century Jewish sense; (2) Judaism was not monolithic—some streams more “legalistic”; (3) even Sanders’s covenant nomism requires law-keeping to “stay in” and be “declared in” at judgment—underplayed by Sanders and many followers.
- **quote:** "even Sanders’s “covenant nomism” assumes that doing the law was necessary for salvation… to “stay in” and, more importantly, to be “declared in” at the time of the judgment."
- **locus:** L15677
- **passage:** (note on Intro: New Perspective)

### C-R7-008
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo flags tension in Dunn: justification-by-faith-alone language can sound Lutheran, yet Dunn sometimes decouples that broad point from the polemic against works of the law (proselyte boundary vs grace/achievement).
- **quote:** "he decouples this point from Paul’s polemic against works of the law, arguing that the broader theological point is grounded rather in a separate line of reasoning"
- **locus:** L15681
- **passage:** (note on Intro: Dunn / justification)

### C-R7-009
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]

## Coverage summary

**What dominated:** Introduction notes are the densest high-value material—destination/date and Acts–Paul chronology, agitator identity, and especially the **New Perspective / works of the law / justification** cluster (covenant nomism, Dunn/Wright tensions, believing vs doing, already/not-yet justification). Closely related is a long **pistis Christou** apparatus (objective vs subjective, early Greek tradition, rhetorical pairing with ἔργων νόμου, Gen 15:6 against sustained Christ-faithfulness readings).

**Passage notes:** Substantive notes continue on Gal 1 (conversion language, Arabia/Isa 42, missing thanksgiving), Gal 2 (false brothers ≠ Acts 15:5 believers; Antioch and circumcision; Reformers on works of law; Moo’s own pistis Christou shift; DSS parallels), Gal 3 (curse/Lev 18:5; against Martyn’s anti-salvation-history extreme), Gal 4 (**stoicheia** lexical options; calendar; Hagar allegory method), Gal 5 (future righteousness without denying present justification; law of Christ options later), Gal 6 (**Israel of God** alternatives).

**What was largely skipped (by design):** Pure bibliographic “see X 1990” strings, routine grammar notes (participle aspect, δέ discourse function, etc.) without theological payoff, and exhaustive lexical lists that only map occurrence without argument. Text-critical decisions are thin in this Notes block; controversy depth is concentrated in Intro + 2:16 + 3:10–12 + 6:16.
